newsitem.title: USA: Detroit Purchasing Managers May index falls.
newsitem.headline: Detroit Purchasing Managers May index falls.

text.p: The National Association of Purchasing Management-Metro Detroit's composite May index fell to 46.9 from 55.5 in April, accoridng to a Comerica Inc survey released Monday.
An index below 50 signals a slowing manufacturing economy, while a reading above 50 suggests expansion, according to the survey of southeastern Michigan's industrial economy.
The prices paid index was 51.4 in May versus 60.0 in April. The employment component of the barometer was 51.4 in May versus 53.8 in April.
David L. Littmann, senior economist with Detroit-based Comerica Bank, said the decrease reflects auto industry strikes from April.
"This was our first index reading below the 50 point mark in 16 months, since December 1995," he said.
However, May's decline showed up in reduced orders and production levels in both the auto and non-auto sectors. The sharpest fall occurred in inventories within the non-auto sector, he said.
